title: Update 1.1: December Plans
description: A preview of the next major update. Planned, not released.

sections.heading: December update plans
paragraphs: The October 30 announcement targets update 1.1 for December 2026. Planned work includes production machinery, materials, tools, upgrades, building and automation progression, alongside performance improvements. No exact release day is announced.

sections.heading: Launch figures and scope
paragraphs: The developer reports 600,000 players and approximately 70,000 concurrent players at peak. These are announcement-time figures, not live counts. Late-game progression is a focus; teased future possibilities are not treated here as confirmed released content.

title: Patch 1.0.5: Building & Automation
description: Move structures, build on dusty ground and improve capsule delivery.

sections.heading: Building and placement
paragraphs: Build on dusty terrain and around foundations; move structures with R, cancel with right mouse and remove with X. Demolition now refunds 100%. Middle mouse copies rotation and style. Machine grid spacing is 0.5 m, with free-placement controls.

sections.heading: Automation and world capacity
paragraphs: Catcher groups use a 100 m range and an 80% fill threshold. Garage silos display outfeed problems. The world capsule ceiling rises from 10,000 to 90,000. Large-base packing and Auto-Packer failures are fixed.

sections.heading: Stability and multiplayer
paragraphs: Loading freezes, world-exit memory leaks, construction-related leaks and garbage-collection stutters receive fixes. Public-game warnings, voice-volume controls and vehicle-camera options are added. Region payout, teleport launches, placement and controller-input bugs are addressed.

title: Patch 1.0.4: Robots, Backups & Co-op
description: Robot delivery improvements, night vision and automatic backups.

sections.heading: Robots, map and lighting
paragraphs: Night Vision Goggles cost $350 and join the N lighting cycle. Map waypoints, station teleport controls and robot filters improve navigation. J.O.O.N.A.S. sends capsules without its former docking sequence, works away from players, replans around obstacles and shows a full-bin warning.

sections.heading: Backups and compatibility
paragraphs: Each save slot keeps five rotating backups. The first occurs after one minute, then every 30 minutes. Backups are outside Steam Cloud. Saving, quitting and damaged-save recovery improve; saves written by 1.0.4 cannot open in older builds.

sections.heading: Belts and platform fixes
paragraphs: Mergers alternate inputs, and crewmates can attach belt forks. Ground synchronization, stalled packing, foundations and robot paths receive fixes. Proton startup is repaired; AMD defaults to DirectX 11, with DirectX 12 available as a launch option.

title: Patch 1.0.3: Shared Upgrades & Delivery
description: Crew-wide upgrades, host controls and belt-fed deposit fixes.

sections.heading: Shared progression and host controls
paragraphs: The host’s Upgrade Matrix becomes crew-wide. Crew members can purchase shared upgrades, with previous progress reconciled. Hosts gain kick, ban and unban controls under Your Crew; everyone must use the same patch.

sections.heading: Belts, placement and selling
paragraphs: Dust and stone entering the collector by belt pay immediately. Carried capsules can be placed where aimed. Forks snap between ports and machines can cross foundations. Multiplayer forks receive fixes.

sections.heading: Vehicles, saves and performance
paragraphs: Any garage can manage owned vehicles. Removing a garage preserves its vehicles. Large-save loading, damaged-save checks and driving/teleport streaming improve. The developer reports frame-rate improvements; this site has not independently benchmarked them.

title: A Message From the Developers
description: The two-person team discusses launch issues, co-op fixes and automation priorities.

sections.heading: Launch priorities
paragraphs: The two-person studio acknowledges crashes, performance problems, co-op issues and uneven automation progression. It describes shared research, save protection, host moderation and belt fixes already shipped.

sections.heading: Work still ahead
paragraphs: The team prioritizes crashes, robots stopping when players leave and automation balance. This is a development-status letter, not a separate numbered patch or a promise that every issue has been resolved.
